candidate.answerReason: The zero dot product makes the line's direction perpendicular to the plane's normal. The line is therefore parallel to the plane or contained in it, and containment is explicitly excluded.

methods.label: Direction-normal parallelism criterion
methods.explanation: The direction is perpendicular to the normal vector, indicating that the line has no inclination toward intersecting the plane. Since it is also known not to lie in the plane, it is parallel to the plane.
methods.levelReason: The direction-normal criterion and the distinction between parallelism and containment are part of high-school spatial geometry.
